## Homework Week 07 (Maps)

*Loading libraries*

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| messgae: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(lubridate)
library(tidytuesdayR)
library(maps)
library(mapdata)
library(mapproj)
library(plotly)
```

*Loading TidyTuesday Bigfoot data*

```{r}
#| message: false

tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2022, week = 37) 
# ^ tidytuesday data requires you to load in both the dfs of the week
# v and read in the dataset you're interested in
bigfoot <- tuesdata$bigfoot
```

*Take a peek at the data*
```{r}
str(bigfoot)

glimpse(bigfoot)
```
It seems like the only data we're gonna need are the county/state data. The lat/long/geohash columns contain a lot of NAs. A heatmap of the counties will cover more observations and still provide a "useful" visualization.

### Building the maps() polygon
```{r}
state <- map_data("state")
county <- map_data("county")
```

### Organizing Data
```{r}
#dropping entries we don't need for mapping
small_bigfoot <- bigfoot |>
  select(county, state, season) |>
  #filtering out all the other columns we don't need
  drop_na() |> #cleaning out NAs
  filter(!grepl("Unknown", season)) |> #NAs in season are set as Unknown :eyeroll:
  mutate(region = str_to_lower(state), #making all the state and county names lowercase
         subregion = str_to_lower(county),
         subregion = str_remove_all(subregion, "county"), #removing the extraneous "county" from the end of every entry
         subregion = str_trim(subregion)) |> #gets rid of extra spaces
  group_by(region, subregion, season) |> #grouping by the tidier columns
  mutate(obs_count = n()) |> #get an obs count, our actual thing we're plotting by
  select(-c(county, state)) #send old columns to the farm upstate
```

### Merging Tidy Data with Map Data
```{r}
#| messgae: false
table_bigfoot <- small_bigfoot |> #Adding my data to the county data so it works with Maps
  inner_join(county, relationship = "many-to-many") #the warning message said to this relationship part

```


### Plotting Data
```{r}

#In order for ggplotly() to work, we must first make a ggplot object
plot_bigfoot <-  ggplot() +
  
    geom_polygon(data = state, #creating a base map so gaps in the bigfoot df aren't just nothing
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group, #DON'T FORGET THIS
                   fill = region),
               color = "black",
               fill = "navyblue",
               alpha = 0.1) +
  
    geom_polygon(data = table_bigfoot, #plotting our mashed-up bigfoot and county map data
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group, #ABSOLUTELY NO FORGETTING THIS
                   fill = obs_count,
                   frame = season), #this part doesn't load when making the object, but ggplotly will read it later
                    ) +
    theme_void() + #banish all axis labels and titles
  
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "bisque", high = "brown") +
    labs(dictionary = c( #making a dictionary of terms that need to be modified
      obs_count = "Sightings",
      season = "Season",
      region = "State",
      subregion = "County"),
         title = "Sasquatch Sightings Over Seasons")

ggplotly(plot_bigfoot)
    
  


```
